newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia bus plunges into ravine, 23 injured.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia bus plunges into ravine, 23 injured.

text.p: At least 23 people were injured when a bus plunged into a ravine near the Malaysian hilltop resort of Genting Highlands, the national Bernama news agency said early on Tuesday.
It said it had no immediate word on whether anyone had been killed in the accident, the second of its kind this year.
The accident took place around 2300 hours (1500 GMT) on Monday, the news agency said, quoting a police spokesman.

The bus ran off the winding road leading from a highway to the resort, the news agency said. Genting Highlands is located nearly 6,000 feet (1,830 metres) above sea level about 60 km (40 miles) from the capital Kuala Lumpur.
The 23 injured were being treated at two hospitals at the resort and in Kuala Lumpur, Bernama quoted police as saying. The agency had no word on the extent of the injuries.
On July 16, a bus carrying tourists plunged 120 metres (yards) into a ravine along the Genting road killing 17 people and injuring at least 15.
On June 30, 1995, a landslide along the road to the resort killed at least 21 people and injured 22.
